headline: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced a new four-star command for autonomous drones and AI and said the number of top generals and admirals is being cut by 20%.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered to 4: the speech was on 30 Sep 2026, our 1 Oct edition carried the new command, and ABC's account adds the 20% cut but no new step today.
importance_line: Senior officers and the troops they lead are affected first, then drone and AI contractors that would supply the new command, and the debate over civilian control of the military, but ABC gives no size, budget or commander for the command and the cuts are Hegseth's own account.
summary: ABC News reports that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, in a 'State of the Force' speech at Quantico, Virginia, on Wednesday 30 Sep 2026, announced AUTOWARCOM, a four-star Autonomous Warfighting Command meant to bring fast-developing drone technology and AI into the force, and said 20% of general and admiral posts are being cut, which he said the media call a purge but he calls accountability. Our 1 Oct 2026 edition carried the new command; the other announcements in ABC's account include a religious affairs office, military bases that generate their own power, and a study group with Elon Musk and Palmer Luckey of defence-technology company Anduril.
notes: Stale: ABC says 'Wednesday' without a date; 30 Sep 2026 is inferred because our 1 Oct 2026 edition (item 68) carried DefenseScoop's 30 Sep report of the same AUTOWARCOM announcement, and a 6 Oct report (The Defense Post, 7 Oct pool item C13-03) followed. Status CONFIRMED because it is the secretary's own on-record speech. The article also reports, citing people familiar, that then-Army Secretary Dan Driscoll warned the White House that removing senior officers was thinning the Army's leadership; not in the summary.
